meta.title: Open Doors — where the path is clear, and where it is not
meta.grain: one row per people group x country
meta.the_question: Every other table answers SUPPLY (does a resource exist, is there internet). This answers ROUTE: could a person here reach the gospel in their own language today?
meta.boundary: This table records resource AVAILABILITY and network ROUTE only. It never indicates believers, churches or meeting points, and path-open never means the gospel has arrived.
meta.verdicts: channel-open-no-resource (highest translation leverage) · resource-exists-channel-shut (a DISTRIBUTION problem, not a translation one) · no-resource-and-no-channel · resource-and-channel-but-network-poor · channel-UNMEASURED (no probe coverage — an UNKNOWN, never read as censorship) · path-open.
meta.honesty: not-measured platforms are counted SEPARATELY and never as open or shut. Rows carry channels_not_measured + a confidence_note so a verdict resting on partial data says so.
meta.derived_from: gospel-access-vs-growth + platform-reachability + connectivity-by-country. NO new research — a join over already-verified tables.

rows.open_channels: WhatsApp, WeChat, Signal, Messenger, Viber, Line
rows.action: HIGHEST TRANSLATION LEVERAGE: the road is open and there is nothing to send. A resource made here can actually arrive.
rows.what_this_does_NOT_say: This is a SUPPLY-and-ROUTE reading only. It never indicates believers, churches, meeting points, or that anyone has received anything. path-open means a route is technically clear, NOT that the gospel has arrived.
rows.source: DERIVED — gospel-access-vs-growth + platform-reachability + connectivity-by-country. No new research.
